target: Penerbangan kami ditunda dua jam, padahal kami sudah tiba di bandara sejak subuh.
english: Our flight is delayed two hours, even though we already arrived at the airport at dawn.
grammar: Padahal = even though / and yet: padahal kami sudah tiba = even though we had already arrived.

target: Menurut petugas maskapai, pesawat pengganti baru mendarat jam sembilan malam.
english: According to the airline staff, the replacement plane only lands at nine in the evening.

target: Kami hampir saja ketinggalan pesawat sambungan di Jakarta tadi siang.
english: We very nearly missed the connecting flight in Jakarta earlier this afternoon.
grammar: Hampir saja = very nearly (a close call): hampir saja ketinggalan = very nearly missed it.

target: Para penumpang tujuan Denpasar dimohon segera menuju pintu tujuh.
english: Passengers bound for Denpasar are requested to proceed to gate seven immediately.
grammar: Dimohon = are requested to, the announcement passive: para penumpang dimohon = passengers are requested.

target: Meskipun antrean transit panjang, kami masih sempat mengejar penerbangan berikutnya.
english: Even though the transit line was long, we still managed to catch the next flight.

target: Yang paling melelahkan dari perjalanan ini adalah menunggu enam jam di bandara.
english: The most tiring part of this trip is waiting six hours at the airport.
grammar: Yang X adalah Y spotlights one thing: Yang paling melelahkan adalah menunggu = the most tiring part is the waiting.

target: Koper saya sempat hilang di bandara transit, tapi akhirnya ditemukan.
english: My suitcase was lost for a while at the transit airport, but it was finally found.

target: Petugas bilang bahwa koper yang rusak bisa diganti oleh maskapai.
english: The staff member said that a damaged suitcase can be replaced by the airline.

target: Jangan-jangan koper kita masuk ke pesawat yang salah lagi.
english: I'm afraid our suitcase may have gone onto the wrong plane again.
grammar: Jangan-jangan voices a worry: jangan-jangan masuk pesawat yang salah = what if it got on the wrong plane.

target: Kami mohon pengertian Bapak dan Ibu atas keterlambatan penerbangan sore ini.
english: We ask for your understanding, ladies and gentlemen, for this afternoon's flight delay.

target: Antrean di imigrasi pagi ini makan waktu hampir dua jam.
english: The line at immigration this morning took up almost two hours.
grammar: Makan waktu = eats time, i.e. takes long: makan waktu dua jam = takes up two hours.

target: Pesawat sudah penuh, sehingga kami dipindahkan ke penerbangan sore tanpa biaya tambahan.
english: The plane was already full, so we were moved to the afternoon flight at no extra charge.

target: Petugas bertanya apakah kami mau menunggu atau minta uangnya dikembalikan.
english: The staff member asked whether we wanted to wait or ask for the money back.

target: Penumpang yang pesawatnya dibatalkan boleh menginap di hotel yang dibayar maskapai.
english: Passengers whose plane was canceled may stay overnight in a hotel paid for by the airline.

target: Tagihan kami naik dua ratus ribu, padahal kami tidak membuka minibar sama sekali.
english: Our bill went up two hundred thousand, even though we didn't open the minibar at all.

target: Resepsionis bilang bahwa biaya sarapan sudah termasuk dalam harga kamar.
english: The receptionist said that the breakfast cost is already included in the room price.

target: Kami sudah selesai berkemas, tinggal menunggu uang jaminan dikembalikan.
english: We have finished packing; all that's left is waiting for the deposit to be returned.
grammar: Tinggal + verb = all that's left is: tinggal menunggu = just waiting now.

target: Mohon dicek kembali, sepertinya kami ditagih dua kali untuk malam terakhir.
english: Please check again; it seems we were charged twice for the last night.

target: Yang membuat kami kecewa adalah biaya tambahan yang muncul tanpa penjelasan.
english: What makes us disappointed is the extra charge that appeared without explanation.

target: Kami minta check-out lebih siang, namun sistem tetap menagih biaya satu malam penuh.
english: We asked for a later check-out, yet the system still charged the cost of one full night.

target: Seandainya kami tahu kolam renangnya berbayar, kami pasti memilih hotel lain.
english: If we had known the swimming pool cost extra, we would certainly have chosen another hotel.
grammar: Seandainya = if only / supposing (unreal): seandainya kami tahu = if we had known.

target: Manajer akhirnya turun tangan setelah kami menunggu satu jam di lobi.
english: The manager finally stepped in after we waited an hour in the lobby.
grammar: Turun tangan = to step in personally: manajer turun tangan = the manager steps in himself.

target: Menurut resepsionis, uang jaminan kembali ke kartu kami dalam tujuh hari.
english: According to the receptionist, the deposit returns to our card within seven days.

target: Kami terlanjur membayar tagihan itu sebelum melihat ada biaya aneh.
english: We had already paid that bill before seeing there was a strange charge.
grammar: Terlanjur = already done, too late to undo: terlanjur membayar = already paid before realizing.

target: Biaya laundry yang tidak pernah kami pesan itu akhirnya dihapus dari tagihan.
english: That laundry charge we never ordered was finally removed from the bill.

target: Dengan senang hati kami kirimkan rincian tagihan ke email Bapak.
english: With pleasure, we will send the bill details to your email, sir.

target: Kamarnya bagus, tapi proses check-out lama sekali sampai kami hampir terlambat.
english: The room was nice, but the check-out process was so long that we were almost late.

target: Mudah-mudahan hotel ini memperbaiki sistem tagihannya sebelum kami datang lagi.
english: Hopefully this hotel fixes its billing system before we come again.

target: Katanya pantai di ujung desa ini lebih sepi daripada pantai utama.
english: They say the beach at the end of this village is quieter than the main beach.
grammar: Katanya = they say / I heard: katanya lebih sepi = I hear it's quieter.

target: Semakin lama tinggal di sini, semakin berat rasanya untuk pulang.
english: The longer we stay here, the harder it feels to go home.
grammar: Semakin X, semakin Y = the more X, the more Y: semakin lama, semakin berat = the longer, the harder.

target: Jangan lupa beli buah tangan untuk keluarga sebelum pulang ke negara kamu.
english: Don't forget to buy souvenirs for the family before going home to your country.
grammar: Buah tangan = hand fruit, a small gift from a trip: beli buah tangan = buy souvenirs.

target: Kalau boleh tahu, Ibu sudah berapa lama tinggal di desa ini?
english: If I may ask, how long have you lived in this village, ma'am?

target: Siapa tahu tahun depan kami bisa kembali ke pulau ini lagi.
english: Who knows, maybe next year we can come back to this island again.
grammar: Siapa tahu = who knows, maybe: siapa tahu kami bisa kembali = who knows, we might come back.

target: Di sini orang santai soal waktu, kami menyebutnya jam karet.
english: Here people are relaxed about time; we call it rubber time.
grammar: Jam karet = rubber time, the famously stretchy attitude to schedules across Indonesia.

target: Sambil menunggu hujan reda, kami mengobrol dengan pemilik warung kopi.
english: While waiting for the rain to ease, we chatted with the coffee stall owner.

target: Menurut warga di sini, air terjun itu paling indah waktu musim hujan.
english: According to the residents here, that waterfall is most beautiful during the rainy season.

target: Walaupun bahasa Indonesia saya masih kacau, orang di sini sabar sekali.
english: Even though my Indonesian is still a mess, people here are very patient.

target: Yang membuat kami betah di sini adalah orangnya yang ramah dan santai.
english: What makes us feel at home here is the people, who are friendly and relaxed.

target: Kami mulai terbiasa makan pakai tangan seperti orang lokal di warung.
english: We are starting to get used to eating with our hands like locals at food stalls.

target: Semoga besok cerah supaya kalian bisa melihat matahari terbit dari bukit.
english: Hopefully tomorrow is clear so you all can see the sunrise from the hill.

target: Kami capek setengah mati setelah mendaki gunung itu semalaman.
english: We are dead tired after climbing that mountain all night.
grammar: Setengah mati = half dead, i.e. extremely: capek setengah mati = dead tired.

target: Pemilik penginapan berjanji akan mengantar kami ke pelabuhan besok pagi.
english: The guesthouse owner promised to take us to the harbor tomorrow morning.

target: Menurut saya, rencana peluncuran ini terlalu cepat untuk tim kecil kita.
english: In my opinion, this launch plan is too fast for our small team.
grammar: Menurut saya = in my opinion: menurut saya terlalu cepat = in my view it's too fast.

target: Saya rasa usul dari tim pemasaran itu masuk akal juga.
english: I feel that suggestion from the marketing team makes sense too.

target: Bapak dan Ibu sekalian, rapat kita mulai dengan laporan penjualan bulan lalu.
english: Ladies and gentlemen, we begin our meeting with last month's sales report.
grammar: Sekalian after Bapak dan Ibu addresses the whole room: Bapak dan Ibu sekalian = ladies and gentlemen.

target: Saya setuju dengan idenya, namun anggaran kita belum tentu cukup.
english: I agree with the idea; however, our budget is not necessarily enough.

target: Yang perlu kita putuskan hari ini adalah tanggal peluncuran produk baru.
english: What we need to decide today is the launch date of the new product.

target: Kalau menurut Bapak, bagian mana yang paling berisiko dari rencana ini?
english: In your opinion, sir, which part of this plan is the riskiest?

target: Sebelum memutuskan, kita coba dengarkan dulu pendapat tim lapangan.
english: Before deciding, let's first hear out the field team's opinion.
grammar: Coba before a verb softens it into a suggestion: kita coba dengarkan = let's just hear them out.

target: Datanya menarik, akan tetapi kesimpulannya masih terlalu berani menurut saya.
english: The data is interesting; however, the conclusion is still too bold in my opinion.

target: Dia selalu mencari muka di depan direktur setiap kali rapat besar.
english: He always sucks up in front of the director every time there's a big meeting.
grammar: Mencari muka = to seek face, i.e. to suck up: mencari muka di depan bos = curry favor with the boss.

target: Usul yang kamu tolak kemarin itu justru dipuji oleh kantor pusat.
english: The suggestion you rejected yesterday was actually praised by the head office.

target: Mohon pendapat Ibu tentang rencana anggaran yang kami kirim kemarin.
english: We request your opinion, ma'am, on the budget plan we sent yesterday.

target: Kami sempat membahas ide itu tahun lalu, tapi akhirnya berhenti di tengah jalan.
english: We did discuss that idea last year, but it eventually stopped midway.

target: Seandainya semua divisi setuju, proyek ini bisa dimulai bulan depan.
english: If all divisions agreed, this project could be started next month.

target: Sebagian tim mendukung usul itu, sedangkan sisanya masih ragu-ragu.
english: Part of the team supports that suggestion, whereas the rest are still hesitant.
grammar: Sedangkan contrasts two halves: A mendukung, sedangkan B ragu = A supports it, whereas B has doubts.

target: Semakin dekat tenggat, semakin sering klien mengubah permintaan mereka.
english: The closer the deadline, the more often the client changes their requests.

target: Klien minta supaya laporan akhir dikirim hari Kamis, bukan hari Jumat.
english: The client asks that the final report be sent on Thursday, not Friday.

target: Padahal timnya tinggal dua orang, target bulan ini malah dinaikkan.
english: Even though the team is down to two people, this month's target was raised instead.

target: Kami gagal mengejar tenggat kemarin karena data dari cabang datang terlambat.
english: We failed to catch yesterday's deadline because the data from the branch arrived late.

target: Kalau saja tenggatnya mundur seminggu, hasilnya pasti jauh lebih rapi.
english: If only the deadline moved back a week, the result would surely be far neater.
grammar: Kalau saja = if only (wishing things were different): kalau saja tenggatnya mundur = if only the deadline slipped.

target: Dengan hormat, kami memohon perpanjangan waktu sampai akhir bulan ini.
english: Respectfully, we request an extension of time until the end of this month.
grammar: Dengan hormat = respectfully, the standard opener of formal letters and requests.

target: Laporannya hampir selesai, tinggal menunggu angka terakhir dari bagian keuangan.
english: The report is almost finished; all that's left is waiting for the final numbers from finance.

target: Atasan saya berjanji akan bicara dengan klien soal jadwal yang mustahil itu.
english: My boss promised to talk with the client about that impossible schedule.

target: Lembur sampai tengah malam sudah jadi makanan sehari-hari di tim kami.
english: Working overtime until midnight has become daily fare on our team.

target: Yang membuat jadwal ini berantakan adalah permintaan tambahan yang datang setiap minggu.
english: What makes this schedule a mess is the additional requests that come every week.

target: Kami berani berjanji selesai hari Jumat asalkan tidak ada permintaan baru lagi.
english: We dare to promise it's done by Friday as long as there are no more new requests.
grammar: Asalkan = as long as, provided that: asalkan tidak ada permintaan baru = provided nothing new is added.

target: Tim desain terpaksa berhenti mengerjakan proyek lain demi tenggat ini.
english: The design team is forced to stop working on other projects for the sake of this deadline.

target: Mudah-mudahan revisi kali ini benar-benar revisi yang terakhir.
english: Hopefully this revision really is the last revision.

target: Katanya direktur sudah setuju tenggatnya digeser ke awal bulan depan.
english: Word is the director has agreed the deadline be shifted to early next month.

target: Internet kantor mati sejak pagi, sehingga rapat online kami pindah ke kafe.
english: The office internet has been down since morning, so our online meeting moved to a cafe.

target: Saya sedang asyik menulis laporan waktu laptop tiba-tiba mati total.
english: I was deep in writing the report when the laptop suddenly died completely.
grammar: Sedang asyik + verb = absorbed in doing it: sedang asyik menulis = deep in writing.

target: Kata bagian IT, server kantor baru normal lagi besok siang.
english: According to the IT department, the office server will only be back to normal tomorrow afternoon.

target: Saya angkat tangan kalau disuruh memperbaiki printer tua itu lagi.
english: I give up if I'm told to fix that old printer again.
grammar: Angkat tangan = raise your hands, i.e. give up: saya angkat tangan = I give up.

target: File yang kamu cari itu sudah saya pindahkan ke folder bersama.
english: That file you're looking for, I have already moved to the shared folder.
grammar: Object + saya + bare verb is the polished passive: sudah saya pindahkan = I have moved it.

target: Biasakan menyimpan pekerjaan setiap beberapa menit karena listrik sering padam.
english: Make it a habit to save your work every few minutes because the power often goes out.

target: Aplikasi barunya memang canggih, namun banyak rekan belum terbiasa memakainya.
english: The new app is indeed sophisticated; however, many colleagues aren't used to using it yet.

target: Semoga kata sandi baru ini tidak saya lupakan seperti yang kemarin.
english: Hopefully I won't forget this new password like the one before.

target: Bagian IT bertanya apakah masalah email kamu sudah beres atau belum.
english: The IT department asked whether your email problem is sorted out yet or not.

target: Baik laptop lama maupun laptop baru sama-sama lambat kalau membuka aplikasi itu.
english: Both the old laptop and the new laptop are equally slow when opening that app.
grammar: Baik A maupun B = both A and B: baik lama maupun baru sama-sama lambat = old and new are equally slow.

target: Panggilan videonya sempat terputus tiga kali karena sinyal naik turun.
english: The video call briefly cut out three times because the signal kept going up and down.

target: Kami sampaikan bahwa sistem absensi baru mulai dipakai hari Senin depan.
english: We hereby announce that the new attendance system starts being used next Monday.

target: Anak magang itu sekarang jadi tangan kanan kepala bagian IT.
english: That intern is now the right hand of the head of the IT department.
grammar: Tangan kanan = right hand, the most trusted helper: tangan kanan kepala bagian = the boss's right-hand person.

target: Seandainya kantor kita pindah ke sistem baru, semua data lama harus disalin dulu.
english: If our office moved to the new system, all the old data would have to be copied first.

target: Adik saya bilang bahwa dia kadang merasa kesepian di perantauan.
english: My younger sibling says that he sometimes feels lonely living away from home.

target: Ibu berhenti bertanya soal nilai setelah melihat wajah lelah adik saya.
english: Mom stopped asking about grades after seeing my younger sibling's tired face.

target: Ayah jarang bicara soal perasaannya, padahal dia orang yang paling peduli.
english: Dad rarely talks about his feelings, even though he is the person who cares the most.

target: Jangan berkecil hati, nilai satu ujian tidak menentukan masa depan kamu.
english: Don't be discouraged; the grade of one exam doesn't determine your future.
grammar: Berkecil hati = small-hearted, i.e. discouraged: jangan berkecil hati = don't lose heart.

target: Semoga kakak cepat pulih dan bisa berkumpul lagi dengan kita waktu Lebaran.
english: Hopefully my older sibling recovers soon and can gather with us again at Lebaran.

target: Yang paling ibu khawatirkan adalah pola tidur kamu yang berantakan.
english: What Mom worries about most is your messy sleep schedule.

target: Nenek mulai betah di rumah baru walaupun jauh dari cucu-cucunya.
english: Grandma is starting to feel at home in the new house even though it's far from her grandchildren.

target: Kata ibu, ayah diam-diam bangga sekali dengan pekerjaan baru kamu.
english: According to Mom, Dad is secretly very proud of your new job.

target: Kalau saja rumah kita lebih dekat, aku bisa menengok mama setiap minggu.
english: If only our houses were closer, I could visit Mom every week.

target: Sejak menang lomba itu, sepupu saya jadi sedikit besar kepala.
english: Since winning that competition, my cousin has become a little big-headed.
grammar: Besar kepala = big-headed, arrogant: jadi besar kepala setelah menang = got cocky after winning.

target: Ayah pura-pura sibuk membaca koran supaya tidak terlihat menangis di pernikahan kakak.
english: Dad pretended to be busy reading the paper so he wouldn't be seen crying at big sister's wedding.
grammar: Pura-pura + verb = to pretend: pura-pura sibuk membaca = pretending to be busy reading.

target: Aku senang kamu mau jujur soal perasaan kamu, walaupun ceritanya berat.
english: I'm glad you're willing to be honest about your feelings, even though the story is heavy.

target: Anak yang dulu takut gelap itu sekarang berani tidur sendiri di kamarnya.
english: The child who used to be afraid of the dark now dares to sleep alone in his room.

target: Kami sekeluarga mengucapkan selamat atas kelahiran putri pertama kalian.
english: Our whole family congratulates you on the birth of your first daughter.

target: Nenek tetap memasak rendang sendiri walaupun banyak yang menjualnya dekat rumah.
english: Grandma still cooks rendang herself even though many people sell it near the house.

target: Semakin tua, ayah semakin suka makanan pahit seperti pare.
english: The older he gets, the more Dad likes bitter food like bitter gourd.

target: Menurut anak-anak, makanan cepat saji lebih enak daripada sayur bening buatan ibu.
english: According to the kids, fast food tastes better than Mom's clear vegetable soup.

target: Adik bungsu malas mencoba makanan baru kalau bentuknya aneh.
english: The youngest sibling is reluctant to try new food if its shape looks strange.

target: Sambal buatan ibu memang tidak ada duanya di keluarga kami.
english: Mom's homemade sambal truly has no equal in our family.
grammar: Tidak ada duanya = there is no second one, i.e. one of a kind: sambal ibu tidak ada duanya.

target: Kakek tidak suka makanan pedas, sedangkan cucu-cucunya berlomba menambah sambal.
english: Grandpa doesn't like spicy food, whereas his grandchildren compete to add more sambal.

target: Siapa tahu adik mau makan sayur kalau dia ikut memasaknya.
english: Who knows, maybe the little one will want to eat vegetables if he helps cook them.

target: Kata dokter, kakek harus mengurangi gula dalam kopi dan teh manisnya.
english: According to the doctor, Grandpa has to cut down the sugar in his coffee and sweet tea.

target: Makanan yang paling sering diminta cucu-cucu adalah ayam goreng buatan nenek.
english: The food most often requested by the grandchildren is Grandma's fried chicken.

target: Ibu berhasil membuat adik mau makan ikan dengan mencampurnya ke nasi goreng.
english: Mom managed to get the little one to eat fish by mixing it into fried rice.

target: Nasi sudah menjadi bubur, kue ulang tahunnya terlanjur gosong.
english: The rice has turned to porridge — the birthday cake is already burnt beyond saving.
grammar: Nasi sudah menjadi bubur = the rice is already porridge: what's done cannot be undone.

target: Kami sekeluarga baru saja mencoba restoran Korea yang buka dekat rumah.
english: Our whole family just tried the Korean restaurant that opened near the house.

target: Ayah bilang masakan Padang terlalu berminyak, padahal piringnya selalu bersih.
english: Dad says Padang food is too oily, yet his plate is always clean.

target: Mudah-mudahan tahun ini semua sepupu pulang supaya meja makan penuh lagi.
english: Hopefully this year all the cousins come home so the dining table is full again.

target: Kata sepupu, berita yang om kirim di grup itu ternyata hoaks.
english: According to my cousin, the news Uncle sent in the group turned out to be a hoax.

target: Ibu baru belajar memakai stiker, sekarang setiap pesannya penuh stiker bunga.
english: Mom just learned to use stickers; now every message of hers is full of flower stickers.

target: Grup keluarga ramai sekali menjelang Lebaran, sehingga ponsel saya berbunyi terus.
english: The family group gets really busy in the run-up to Lebaran, so my phone keeps buzzing.

target: Foto yang nenek kirim terbalik, tapi tidak ada yang berani memberi tahu beliau.
english: The photo Grandma sent is upside down, but no one dares to tell her.
grammar: Beliau = respectful he/she for elders: memberi tahu beliau = tell her (politely).

target: Ayah bertanya apakah panggilan video hari Minggu jadi atau pindah ke sore.
english: Dad asked whether Sunday's video call is still on or moving to the afternoon.

target: Adik sering membaca pesan grup tanpa pernah membalas satu kata pun.
english: Little brother often reads the group messages without ever replying a single word.
grammar: Pun after a noun stresses not even one: satu kata pun = not even a single word.

target: Setiap pagi grup keluarga banjir ucapan selamat pagi bergambar bunga.
english: Every morning the family group is flooded with good-morning greetings decorated with flowers.
grammar: Banjir used figuratively = flooded with: grup banjir ucapan = the group is flooded with greetings.

target: Jangan-jangan mama salah kirim, foto belanjaan masuk ke grup kantor papa.
english: Mom may well have missent it; the shopping photo went into Dad's office group.

target: Atas nama keluarga besar, kami mengundang semua anggota grup ke syukuran nenek.
english: On behalf of the extended family, we invite all group members to Grandma's thanksgiving celebration.
grammar: Atas nama = on behalf of: atas nama keluarga besar = on behalf of the extended family.

target: Kakak jarang muncul di grup, namun selalu datang kalau ada acara keluarga.
english: Big sister rarely shows up in the group; however, she always comes when there's a family event.

target: Nenek akhirnya berhasil mengirim pesan suara setelah diajari cucunya berkali-kali.
english: Grandma finally managed to send a voice message after being taught by her grandchild many times.

target: Yang paling rajin membalas pesan di grup keluarga justru kakek kami.
english: The one most diligent about replying to messages in the family group is actually our grandpa.

target: Semoga grup keluarga ini tetap ramai sampai cucu-cucu kita besar nanti.
english: May this family group stay lively until our grandchildren are grown someday.
